stimulus.title: Spring Stretch
stimulus.text:
Experiment 1
Students hung a spring from a stand and measured its unstretched length. They hung a mass from the spring, waited for it to stop moving, and measured the new length. The stretch is the difference between the two lengths. Masses were added in steps.
Results (the stretch of the spring): at 100 g, 4.8 cm; at 150 g, 7.2 cm; at 200 g, 9.6 cm; at 250 g, 12.0 cm; at 300 g, 14.4 cm.

stimulus.title: Launch Angle and Range
stimulus.text:
Experiment 1
Students used a spring launcher to fire the same ball at a set angle above the horizontal, always with the spring compressed by the same amount. They measured the horizontal distance from the launcher to the landing point. Each angle was fired three times and the average distance recorded.
Results (the horizontal distance the ball traveled): at 30°, 17.3 m; at 40°, 18.6 m; at 50°, 17.7 m; at 60°, 14.8 m; at 70°, 10.6 m.

stimulus.title: Pendulum Period
stimulus.text:
Experiment 1
Students hung a metal bob from a string, pulled the bob 10° to one side, and released it. They timed 10 complete swings with a stopwatch and divided by 10 to find the period. The procedure was repeated for several string lengths.
Results (the period of the pendulum): at 20 cm, 0.90 s; at 40 cm, 1.28 s; at 60 cm, 1.56 s; at 80 cm, 1.81 s; at 100 cm, 2.02 s; at 120 cm, 2.21 s.

stimulus.title: Solubility and Temperature
